title: Though erased from some Missals, doctors still defend: Damian, Albert, Pelbart, Bustis—Virgin’s empire even over God
source_text: LXV. Ac quanquam ista fuerint ex Missalibus quibusdam erasa, in aliis non ita pridem excusis reposita sunt, & rem ipsam probant ac tuentur non pauci Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae. Sic Cardinalis Damianus de Maria Virgine postea: Accedit, inquit, ad illud aureum divinae majestatis tribunal, non rogans, sed imperans, Domina non ancilla. Sic Albertus Magnus in iis quae Biblia Mariae dicuntur, Maria, inquit, orat ut filia, jubet ut soror, imperat ut mater. Sic Pelbartus Temeswariensis, Vere igitur maximum dominium Beatae Virginis, quae non solum creaturis, sed etiam ipsi Deo tanquam mater filio principatur. Item, Pro salute supplicantium sibi, non solum potest filio supplicare, aliorum Sanctorum more, sed etiam potest filio authoritate materna imperare. Ideo sic Ecclesia orat, Monstra te esse matrem, Quasi diceret Virgini, Imperiose & materna authoritate supplica pro nobis. Sic Denique Bernardinus de Bustis, apud quem haec verba leguntur, Haec est vera propositio, Domini imperio omnia famulantur etiam & Virgo, Et iterum haec est vera, imperio Virginis omnia famulantur etiam Deus.
pass_a_gloss: And although those things were erased from certain Missals, they have been restored in others not so long ago printed, and not a few Doctors of the Roman Church prove and defend the thing itself. Thus Cardinal Damian afterward on the Virgin Mary: She approaches, he says, that golden tribunal of divine majesty, not asking but commanding, Lady not handmaid. Thus Albert the Great in those things which are called Mary’s Bible: Mary, he says, prays as daughter, orders as sister, commands as mother. Thus Pelbart of Temesvár: Truly therefore the greatest dominion of the Blessed Virgin, who is set as prince not only over creatures but even over God Himself as mother over son. Likewise, For the salvation of those who entreat her, she can not only entreat the son after the manner of other Saints, but can also command the son by maternal authority. Therefore the Church thus prays, Show thyself to be a mother, as if it were saying to the Virgin, Imperiously and by maternal authority entreat for us. Thus finally Bernardinus de Bustis, in whom these words are read: This is a true proposition, By the Lord’s empire all things serve even the Virgin also, And again this is true, By the Virgin’s empire all things serve even God.
pass_b_english: Erased from some Missals, restored in others—and many doctors still defend the claim.
Damian: she commands at God’s tribunal as Lady not handmaid; Albert: prays as daughter, commands as mother.
Bustis: ‘By the Virgin’s empire all things serve—even God.’
